title: Trainer bundle
description: The contract between LogParser and the Scoring Trainer. A trainer bundle is manifest.json plus hand chunk files; every file in it validates against this schema. A breaking change bumps the major schemaVersion.

manifest.description: manifest.json: what the bundle holds and where its hands are.

generator.description: The LogParser package and version that built the bundle.

seed.description: Seed of the random draws, so a build can be repeated.

hands.description: Hands in the bundle, each counted once.

drills.description: Hands per drill, by drill key.

chunks.description: The hand chunk files, relative to manifest.json.

drill.description: A drill's key (the trainer translates it) and the IDs of its hands.

handChunk.description: One hand chunk file. Each hand in the bundle appears in exactly one chunk.

hand.description: One scorable win: its tiles, its situation, its answer key and its tags.

tags.description: The hand's tags; empty when it has none. Players never see them before answering; the trainer may show them afterwards, as the lesson.

riichiSticks.description: Riichi sticks on the table when the hand wins.

tsumo.description: True for a win by tsumo, false for ron.

tiles.description: Tiles in mpsz notation: m, p, s for the suits, z for honours (1z East ... 7z Chun), 0 for a red five.

concealed.description: The tiles not part of any call, winning tile included.

calls.description: The hand's calls in the order they were made; empty when it has none. Concealed tiles plus call tiles come to 14, plus one per kan.

uraDoraIndicators.description: Empty unless the hand won with riichi.

call.description: One call. A hand whose only calls are closed kans is closed. Drawing the turned tile is the trainer's job.

tiles.description: All the call's tiles, 3 or 4 of one suit, called and added tiles included. A red five is 0.

calledTile.description: The tile taken from another player's discard. For an added kan, the tile its pon called. Null for a closed kan.

calledFrom.description: Whose discard the called tile was, seen from the winner: kamicha (the player before, on the left), toimen (across) or shimocha (the player after, on the right). A chi is always from kamicha. Null for a closed kan.

answerKey.description: The result Tenhou recorded for the hand, under Tenhou rules.

yaku.description: Each yaku with its han. Every yakuman counts 13 han.

points.description: What the winner receives, before honba and riichi sticks.

payments.description: Who pays the winner what, in points, as Tenhou recorded it. The base payments add up to the points; the honba bonus and the riichi sticks collected are kept apart from them.

base.description: The base payments, split the way the trainer asks for them.

oneOf.description: Ron: one amount from the discarder.
Dealer tsumo: one amount from each player.
Non-dealer tsumo: one amount from the dealer and one from each non-dealer.

honbaBonus.description: The honba bonus the winner collects on top of the base payments: 300 per honba, paid by the discarder on a ron or 100 per honba by each player on a tsumo. In a double ron only the first winner collects it, so the second winner's is 0 even though honba are on the table.

riichiSticksCollected.description: Points from the riichi sticks the winner collects, 1000 per stick. In a double ron only the first winner collects them.

tagKey.description: A tag's key. A tag is a named fact derived from a hand, often a trap a player could fall into; the trainer turns the key into display text. Plain values such as han, fu or yaku are never tags.
